# CASEs with `tags` `individuation`

*Topics — What a work is about. Nucleation holds what the Anthology of the SOTA does not: reading whose subject no anthology topic can hold. The words are seeded from the clusters the reading-time triage of 2026-09-25 found, and grow by decision.*

**Individuation** — what makes something one thing, and the same thing over time or across descriptions — individuation, numerical identity and diversity, individuality and persistence of things of any kind, biological individuality and organisational closure. Selves are self and persons are personhood (group: philosophy; ADR-015, ADR-024).

| [CASE-045](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-045.md) v3 | Measuring the dancing couple: is the pair a nearly decomposable block during the dance and not after it? | A proposed study, not run. Motion-capture several couples dancing an improvised partner dance to recorded music, and record the same people standing and talking after the song. Fit a linear model to the joint kinematics, with the music's beat as an exogenous input. Then ask whether the pair is a block whose gap beats its Occam factor during the dance and not after, whether it compensates under a perturbation, and whether the coupling runs both ways. | Active |
| [CASE-054](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-054.md) | Joking relationships: one kind among the Crow and in Africa with no route between them, descended between Crow and Hidatsa, and a transported tale beside them | Radcliffe-Brown defined the joking relationship as one comparative kind and placed the Crow joking-relative and Dogon and Thonga joking in it; no historical route joins the Crow to West or South-East Africa. Lowie records the same institution among the Hidatsa, a division of the Crow's parent tribe, and Tehrani's phylogeny confirms an Ibo "Little Red Riding Hood" as an oral translation of the European tale. Kind without transport, kind with descent, and a transport, on documented material, for [CLAIM-210](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-210.md). Partial: independence is a fact of geography no source states, and the kind is an analyst's. | Active |
| [CASE-057](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-057.md) | Swapping the two persons of a dyad: nonreciprocal T/V address is changed by the swap and reciprocal address is not, with a constructed French–English dyad and a three-person teasing round | Built on a documented distinction. In Brown and Gilman's account of T/V address, power address is nonreciprocal (the superior says T and receives V) and solidarity address is reciprocal, so swapping the two persons changes the first act and leaves the second fixed. Two constructions extend it. A master-and-servant dyad in French and in modern English is changed by the swap in one realization and fixed by it in the other. A three-person teasing round gives a group whose automorphism can swap characters, so the anchoring of [CLAIM-249](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-249.md) has work to do. | Active |
| [CASE-060](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-060.md) | Two identical unnumbered ballots in one tally: two votes that no relation in the structure of the vote tells apart | Constructed: two voters each put a single cross for the same candidate on identical, unnumbered ballot papers in one box, and both are counted. Within the relations that make a paper a vote, each bears the same relations to everything and none to the other, so they are not even weakly discernible, yet the count is two. Anchored on a documented norm that voids any paper marked so that the voter can be identified (UK RPA 1983, Sch. 1, r. 47(1)(c)). It forces the choice between [CLAIM-136](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-136.md)'s strict and weak versions, and bears on [CLAIM-138](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-138.md). | Active |
| [CASE-076](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-076.md) | Twin pattern-keepers: two systems keep the same pattern, one by its own responses and one through an external controller, and only removing the controller tells them apart | A10 §3.3's paired design, the case behind [QUESTION-086](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-086.md). Matching behaviour and persistence, different organization. Removing the controller destroys one system's pattern and not the other's. A10 then made it harder: the internal regulator at one scale is supported by other processes at another, so which side of the boundary the controller sits on depends on where the boundary is drawn. | Active |
| [CASE-098](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-098.md) | A long rivalry between two teams outlives every player, owner and supporter who first carried it: new fans inherit the antagonism, its history and its practices before they know why the game matters | From U2 of the exchange of 2026-10-16 on sports fandom (the owner's list of subcases). A2's reading: a mature rivalry is "a reproduced intercollective relation", carried by families, media and fan culture, that can survive the replacement of everyone on both sides. Stipulated: the record has no study of a particular rivalry. It shows a relation with its own continuity; it does not show that the relation is a system, an agent, or constitutive of either fandom. | Active |
| [CASE-101](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-101.md) | Three simulated populations with the same turnover and the same aggregate statistics: one whose members respond alike to a common input, one that transmits its norms to its replacements, and one held together by an institution that selects and trains its members | Proposed three times in the exchange of 2026-10-16 (A11 §9, A12 §7 and A13 §5), as the place where criteria of individuality should disagree: Krakauer et al.'s temporal measures, Barnett and Seth's dynamical independence, Hoel's effective information and the block criterion of [CLAIM-157](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-157.md). The common-input arm is Bourrat's "reconstructed entity" ([LIT-005](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-005.md)), which the record already holds and the exchange did not cite. Not run. | Active |
| [CASE-102](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-102.md) | A college program stays good, or bad, at a sport for decades while its whole roster turns over every four or five years | The owner's case, U3 of the exchange of 2026-10-16: "the team composition experiences extremely fast churn, and yet in spite of this real world ship-of-theseus situation, teams often maintain standing on similar timescales as professional teams (if not longer)". A3: it separates the persistence of a collective's identity from the persistence of its capacities, and the second needs a mechanism that regenerates them in each new population. Stipulated: the record holds no data on program persistence. The proposed test is residual persistence of performance across seasons with no player overlap. | Active |
| [CASE-105](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-105.md) | The Washington Senators: the original club became the Minnesota Twins in 1961, an expansion club took its name in Washington and became the Texas Rangers in 1972, and the Montreal Expos became the Washington Nationals in 2005, so franchise, city and supporters each have a different successor | The owner's subcase at U2 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, "the team formerly known as the washington senators". A2 corrected the framing: the name belonged to two franchises, and the city's present team descends from a third. A league can designate the successor franchise; it cannot designate the successor fandom. The lineages are documented; how supporters actually distributed their loyalties is not, and the case does not show that a fandom's identity branched. | Active |
| [CASE-111](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-111.md) | A fold in boundary maintenance: in ḃ = μb + κb² − b³ with cooperative repair (κ > 0), an unmaintained and a maintained state are both stable for −κ²/4 < μ < 0, so maintenance lost past the fold is not restored by returning the parameter, and recovery slows to zero as the fold nears | A7 §4 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, after the owner's "flesh this out further": a normal form for the activity b that maintains a boundary, in which repair processes reinforce one another. Its equilibria, the bistable range, the hysteresis loop and the slowing of recovery at the fold are derived and rechecked here. It shows a capacity to maintain, and not only a state, being lost and not coming back when conditions do, which is [CLAIM-099](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-099.md)'s distinction in a model. A7's own caveat: "This is a proposed minimal model, not an empirical fit." [THEORY-136](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-136.md) and [THEORY-214](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-214.md) say why its early-warning consequence is weak evidence. Fictional by construction. | Active |
| [CASE-115](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-115.md) | Two incompatible quadratic demands on one shared parameter, L₁ = (θ − 1)² and L₂ = (θ + 1)², frustrated at θ = 0 for every update budget, and the split of θ into task-routed θ_A and θ_B that makes both satisfiable | A33 §2 and §5, A35 §3.4 and A38 §4 of the exchange of 2026-10-17. Two demands on one scalar parameter: at θ = 0 the equal-weight gradient vanishes while each loss is 1, no update lowers both, and the local residual is Φ_r = ε for every budget r. A38 splits θ into θ_A and θ_B with the task context routed, and both demands are met at (1, −1). Used for the zero aggregate gradient, the residual, relief judged on the original demands, and differentiation. A38's caveat is kept: the split is "a division of functional jurisdiction", and it "does not automatically mean that two new autonomous individuals have formed". Fictional by construction. | Active |
| [CASE-116](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-116.md) | Three finite-state systems that dissociate slowness, member regeneration and transmission: a slow flip register no member reads (second eigenvalue 0.98), a register members read and rewrite that forgets fast (second eigenvalue 0.2, nonzero intervention effect), and a rule passed through an archive between two episodes that never run together | A3 and A4 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, after the owner's "continue" and "show me". Arm A is slow and not endogenous; arm B is endogenous and not slow; arm C transmits a rule with no continuous operation. The eigenvalues and intervention effects are rechecked here. Arm A shows what [CLAIM-327](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-327.md) and [CLAIM-331](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-331.md) already say in words, that slowness is not sufficient; arm B is the new direction, that slowness is not necessary, and it holds only for weak maintenance, in A4's words. Arm C is [CLAIM-287](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-287.md)'s dormant coalition and does not settle identity. Fictional by construction. | Active |
